argvRule: An empty or missing --repository/--map is stage arguments, invalid-arguments. A missing --expected-base or --target is not an argv error: it reaches authority-arguments after the wire stage. An unreadable map is stage input, map-unavailable.

exit.0: ACCEPT at stage complete; accept true; code null; issueCodes empty.
exit.1: Verification-class REJECT (stages binding, verification, drift); accept false; code null; one code in issueCodes.
exit.2: Wire REJECT (code set, accept false) or any operational UNSUPPORTED (code set, accept null, assurance null).

stages.rule: Strict JSON before shape; a non-object root is not-an-object; spec before the key-set check. Map-local references are wire checks, with native code names: a duplicate evidence ID, unknown basis or duplicate basis pair is invalid-field, a supported hunk without basis is unsupported-without-basis and an uncited evidence item is orphan-evidence. Counts and witness hunks are reported from a successful decode onward.
Checked after a successful wire decode. Base and target must be full lowercase commit OIDs of one width; otherwise invalid-arguments.

A structural reason with runtime.Version() outside the admitted structural tuples (go1.27.1, and go1.27.2 under decision 0522) refuses with structuralQualification UNSUPPORTED; otherwise a structural map reports EXPERIMENTAL_TUPLE_PENDING_FULL_CORPUS and a nonstructural map NOT_REQUIRED. Windows refuses process containment.
Repository, snapshot, blob and canonical-diff failures keep their inherited operational codes; the listed set is the inherited repository class, not a claim that every code is covered by a vector.
Base sidecar absent or 100644 is allowed; target sidecar absent or an exact 100644 copy of the raw input bytes is allowed.

Patch digest before hunk mapping before evidence before basis and mechanical proof. A map hunk absent from the canonical patch is invalid-field; a canonical patch hunk absent from the map is uncited-hunk, checked after every map hunk. An old/new mode line in the canonical patch is malformed-patch; another unsupported mode is unsupported-tree-mode; both are verification issues, not repository refusals. Inherited public patch-parser codes from the parsed canonical patch are verification issues too. An evidence span with start >= end or end beyond the blob is evidence-unavailable.
stable and relocated accept; stale, ambiguous and deleted refuse. Every record is retained in ascending evidence ID order.

nonClaims: No witness establishes test execution, adequacy, semantic correctness or completion authority.
primary-clean-config-bounded/1 is a limited envelope, not native equivalence.
